newsitem.title: BULGARIA: BULGARIA TO CLOSE SODI DEVNYA DEAL IN 20 DAYS.
newsitem.headline: BULGARIA TO CLOSE SODI DEVNYA DEAL IN 20 DAYS.

text.p: Bulgaria hopes to close a privatisation deal with one of six foreign investors vying for its largest and most profitable chemical complex Sodi Devnya in up to 20 days, a senior government official said on Friday.
"I hope we will be able to announce the results of the tender in the next 15 to 20 days," deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Economy Roumen Gechev told a news conference.
Bids from six big foreign companies were received in the Privatisation Agency by Thursday's tender deadline, Gechev said.
The bidders are South Korea's LG Group, Belgium's Solvay & Cie, Rhone-Poulenc, General Chemical Group and Sulfa Katanz, said Gechev.
Bids containing price offers and business plans for the coming years were opened by a commission consisting of several ministers and privatisation agency executives.
"Investments of between $80 million and $200 million have been pledged over the next three to five years," said Gechev. He gave no more details.

The value of the plant, which exports 10 to 12 percent of the calcinated soda traded in the world, was not announced. Its export markets include the Far East, the Middle East, Latin America and Western Europe.
Sodi-Devnya, which can process 1.2 million tonnes of calcinated soda annually, currently operates at 80 percent of its capacity and its net profit for last year was $3.5 million.
The chemical giant is one of 15 state enterprises, which the government plans to sell by year-end in a bid to raise cash for the country's current expenses and debt payments.
The list also includes a rose-oil distillery in Kazanlak, another big plant producing chemical fertilizers, Himko, and a bio-products producer.
"If we do not sell these companies now, in few years they will turn into museum antiques," said Gechev.
The cash-strapped country can not provide the investments needed for their operation, he said.

Speeding up privatisation and closing down loss-makers are a crucial condition for funding from multilateral lenders. The World Bank and the International Monetary Fund are expected to decide on more Bulgarian funding at the end of this month or in early November. -- Elisaveta Konstantinova, Sofia Newsroom, 359-2-84561
